subject: Interoperate between rapache and Ruby on Rails

messages.author: 9b8e33e6f9d197ef
messages.subject: Interoperate between rapache and Ruby on Rails
parts:
Hello,

I have rapache installed on my system, a Linux box with apache,
passenger and Ruby on Rails.

I've got the "hello world" example (http://labs.dataspora.com/R/
helloworld) working, so I can visit localhost/R/hello and this
generates a nice plot as per the example.

My Ruby on Rails install is also working, so I can visit localhost and
get served a page by RoR. Great.

I'm now somewhat at a loss as to how to generate a graph in R using
data from Ruby on Rails. It seems I have set up two quite unconnected
systems! Does anyone have a pointer on the best way to go from here?

Toby

messages.author: 48f24841e806e6c6
messages.subject: Re: Interoperate between rapache and Ruby on Rails
parts:
Well, there's quite a number of ways one could integrate the two. I've
developed a pure web services way with REDCap, a data collection tool
for researchers:

http://project-redcap.org/

It's written in php and makes web service style calls to rapache,
delivering both graphics and textual summary statistics. Here's a
crude diagram:

php <----> rapache
^
|
|
v
browser

I'll see if I can get permission to post the documentation somewhere
public.

Another way is to use a hybrid approach whereby the web app integrates
the two within the delivered html. I used this approach for the RoR/
rapache polyart app here:

http://polyart.rapache.net/

source here:

http://polyart.rapache.net/polyart_dist.tgz

and the crude diagram is:

RoR <---> rapache
^ A
| /
| /
| /
| /
v A
browser

I'm working off the top of my head here since it's been so long since
I wrote that app, but essentially RoR builds a web page which has html
form elements that posts to rapache, I think there's also javascript
calls as well. Also I believe there are some form posts to RoR which
then call rapache.

Jeff

messages.author: 9b8e33e6f9d197ef
messages.subject: Re: Interoperate between rapache and Ruby on Rails
parts:
I'm looking at your polyart source and trying to modify hello world.
The step up in complexity between the two is rather large, as though
one is "Hello world" and the other is "Create a world" ;).

By following polyart, it seems I should be able to modify the hello
function to accept arguments from the URL like this:

hello <- function(id){
setContentType("text/html")
png("/home/toby/shared_folder/git_proj/Rails/LTS_FrontEnd/public/
hello.png")
plot(sample(10,10),col=1:8,pch=8)
dev.off()
cat("<html>")
cat("<body>")
cat("<h1>hello world</h1>")
cat(id)
cat('<img src="/hello.png"')
cat("</body>")
cat("</html>")
OK
}

but if I visit http://localhost/R/hello?id=10 I get a rapache error:

RApache Warning/Error!!!
Error in cat(id) : argument "id" is missing, with no default

Where am I going wrong?
Thanks,
Toby

messages.author: 25a4f5811cd7d59e
messages.subject: Re: Interoperate between rapache and Ruby on Rails
parts:
You won't add arguments to the function, rather you will find them in
the magic GET variable like so:

hello <- function(){
setContentType("text/html")
id <- GET$id
...
}

Jeff
